summary: Frontend-only testing of the Session Transfer hosted landing page + in-page Web Crypto simulator. All 19 assertions passed. Landing loads with no console errors, hero heading correct, all 7 nav links smooth-scroll, nav/hero/install/footer download buttons all trigger a session-transfer-v1.2.0.zip download, install modal opens+closes, storage matrix renders all rows (including 'By design' WebAuthn/TLS), FAQ accordions expand/collapse. Simulator toggles work, export produces a well-formed one-time transfer code (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX from custom alphabet) and ciphertext preview, wrong code produces real 'Decryption failed' (proves genuine AES-GCM auth), correct code decrypts and shows Decrypted / per-driver 'restored N/N' / Verification passed lines with Browser B status flipping to 'Authenticated'. Zip asset at /session-transfer-v1.2.0.zip returns HTTP 200.
critical_code_review_comments: Simulator import button is disabled when code length < 8; this matches spec (14-char dashed code) but could be surfaced as a hint to users.
Landing.jsx is ~440 lines with many sub-components; consider splitting Nav/Hero/Sections into separate files for maintainability (soft suggestion, not blocking).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Landing page is at https://session-bridge-4.preview.emergentagent.com and is a single-page app. All interactive elements have data-testid. Simulator uses real window.crypto.subtle AES-256-GCM + PBKDF2 (210k iters), so wrong code path genuinely fails to decrypt. Downloads use anchor .download attribute pointing to /session-transfer-v1.2.0.zip in frontend/public. Chrome extension itself is NOT testable in this environment.
